title: Personalization of Basic and Moral Values Guiding LLM-Controlled Assistant Robots
abstract: arXiv:2611.18230v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Personal assistant robots powered by large language models (LLMs) are likely to enter everyday life within the next decade, but the values that should guide their behaviour remain largely unspecified. Current alignment practice steers a single model toward an aggregate of human values, ignoring that individual users may prefer a robot whose value profile differs from their own. We administer parallel self- and robot-targeted versions of three established psycho-metric instruments - the simplified Schwartz Values Survey (SVS), the Portrait Values Questionnaire (PVQ-21), and the Moral Foundations Questionnaire (MFQ) - to potential future users (N=22), capturing both their personal values and the values they would want an assistant robot to embody. We compare the three instruments as personalization tools using the UEQ-S and benchmark fifteen contemporary LLMs against the resulting profiles. Participants wanted their robot to score marked

translated_title: 指导大语言模型控制的助理机器人的基本与道德价值观个性化
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型（LLM）的个人助理机器人很可能在未来十年内进入日常生活，但应当指导其行为的价值观在很大程度上仍未被明确界定。当前的模型对齐实践将单一模型导向人类价值观的总体聚合，却忽略了个体用户可能更希望机器人的价值观特征与自己的有所不同。我们向潜在的未来用户（N=22）发放了三种成熟心理测量工具的平行自评版与机器人定向版——简化版施瓦茨价值观调查（SVS）、肖像价值观问卷（PVQ-21）和道德基础问卷（MFQ），同时捕捉了他们的个人价值观以及他们希望助理机器人所体现的价值观。我们使用UEQ-S比较了这三种工具作为个性化工具的效果，并将十五个当代大语言模型与由此得到的价值观特征进行了基准测试。参与者希望他们的机器人得分明显……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究通过SVS、PVQ-21和MFQ三种心理测量工具发现，用户自身的价值观与他们期望助理机器人体现的价值观存在差异，因此主张对LLM控制的助理机器人进行基本与道德价值观的个性化设定，并基准测试了十五个当代大语言模型。
en_tdlr: This study uses three psychometric instruments (SVS, PVQ-21, and MFQ) to show that users' desired robot value profiles differ from their own personal values, advocating for personalized basic and moral values guiding LLM-controlled assistant robots and benchmarking fifteen contemporary LLMs against these profiles.
